description: Fires when a specific element (e.g. button, form, banner) is present on a page. The trigger runs after the page has fully loaded (DOM is ready). Even if the element is added to the page after initial load (e.g. via JavaScript), the trigger will still detect it and fire. By default the tag fires whenever the selected element is present on any page; add conditions to fire only on specific pages or under specific criteria. See Piwik PRO help: Element presence trigger.

when_to_use: Run a tag when a specific element (banner, form, CTA) appears on the page
Track or act on dynamically injected content that may appear after load
Fire tags only when a given selector is present, with optional page/referrer filters
common_use_cases: Tracking when a specific widget or component is on the page
Conditional tag firing based on element presence plus URL or referrer
best_practices: Use a precise CSS selector (e.g. .promo_banner, #signup-form) to target the element
For domain restrictions use the page_hostname condition reference; for path restrictions use page_path or page_url.

Resolve built-in conditions[].variable_id from trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id before triggers_create — do not guess UUIDs or use variables_list for built-ins
Test that the element is present in the DOM when you expect (including after JS injection)

conditions.description: Array of condition objects. Must include at least one condition that defines which element to watch using the found_elements condition reference with value = CSS selector (e.g. .promo_banner). May include event conditions using trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.

structure.variable_id: Use trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id. Common keys: found_elements, page_hostname, page_path, page_url.
structure.condition_type: equals, contains, is_set, etc.; use once_per_page_view or each_time for Found Elements
structure.value: CSS selector when using Found Elements; hostname (e.g. piwik.pro), path fragment, or URL when using page conditions

conditions.recommendation: Include one found_elements condition with value = your selector. For hostname add page_hostname with condition_type equals. Copy built-in UUIDs from trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id — do not call triggers_create until every variable_id is verified.

element_presence_promo_banner.description: Fire when element matching .promo_banner is present (selector provided via variable)

element_presence_with_page_path.description: Fire when element is present and only on product pages. Page Path variable_id comes from trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.page_path.builtin_variable_id.

element_presence_with_page_hostname.description: Fire when #contact-form is present and only on piwik.pro. Page Hostname variable_id comes from trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.page_hostname.builtin_variable_id.

common_mistakes: Using a selector that never appears in the DOM (e.g. typo or wrong class)
Expecting the trigger to fire before DOM ready (it runs after DOM is ready)
Omitting the element-defining condition so the trigger does not know which element to watch

Using variables_list to resolve built-in event-condition UUIDs instead of trigger_base.json → conditions_reference.conditions.<key>.builtin_variable_id (causes triggers_create retries with wrong variable_id)
Calling triggers_create before copying every built-in conditions[].variable_id from trigger_base.json → conditions_reference — never guess UUIDs

possible_causes: CSS selector does not match any element
Element appears before DOM ready in a way the trigger does not observe
debugging_steps: Verify the selector in browser dev tools (e.g. document.querySelector('.promo_banner'))
Test with fewer or no event conditions
Ensure the element is present after DOM is ready
